main_argument_chains.claim: A circular-transition flat-bottom half-pipe can be parameterized for vertical-air performance.
support_steps: write the energy and loss balance
propagate results to flat width and course length
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Report a complete Question One design vector with explicit parameter handoffs.

main_argument_chains.claim: Changing the objective from vertical air to twist changes the preferred transition angle.
support_steps: map launch components to angular velocity and flight time
reduce the response to the transition angle
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Produce a second design vector whose changed and inherited parameters remain visible.

main_argument_chains.claim: A score-oriented branch can express a compromise between vertical air and rotation.
support_steps: propagate the compromise angle to radius and length
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Present the Question Three vector as a conditional tradeoff result rather than a universal optimum.

main_argument_chains.claim: The design changes systematically with entry speed and is dimensionally comparable with large existing venues.
support_steps: compare modeled and external parameter tables
sweep entry speed over an explicit grid
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use Table 3 as a conditional lookup, while limiting the external claim to dimensional plausibility.

support_steps: state the missing safety measurement relation

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: The labeled geometry diagram establishes height, radius, angle, flat width, and total width before equations.
A local launch diagram makes horizontal and vertical velocity components interpretable.
The response curve visually supports an interior scalar optimum but omits angular units, fixed inputs, and an optimum marker.
Showing both the source accelerometer trace and its simplified law is good transformation disclosure, though points and residuals are absent.
Sketches widen the design discussion but cannot rank shapes without matched geometry and response overlays.
A table plus trend plot supports conditional lookup, but uncertainty and recommendation reversal are absent.
